messages.content: Having issues with this model to recognize driver on the right side. As such driver monitor never engages. Its expecting me to sit on the left side but im on LHD country 🤓

Thank you :YAY:

This morning gWM8 long accelerated into a stop light. It would have slammed into the stopped car at the light if I didn't brake hard. Lightning conditions with the morning sun facing the C3X cameras directly might have confused it.
Lat is mostly good but occasionally it has an uncomfortable right hug. It never hugs left.

mine hugs the inside line on curve.  But yes it is bad in the city, you have to be on-guard.  Sometimes does not resolve a lead properly. It also recognizes intersections before leads, but the problem is that half the time it thinks it is a green light when it is red

Overall I was surprised it drove reasonably well.  Red lights and stop signs are still mostly not working.   It slowed to 3-4 mph for a couple stop signs and if a turn, whip around the corner.   Stop light, I saw it come to a stop, then a second later try to take off again.    Regarding stops, the Off/Dynamic/Predictive (deceleration) setting might be pertinent.  I've lately been running with it off.   Lateral seemed strong as any recent model.   Only notable, uniquely odd thing was a curvy test road I use a lot, first time... this model and in chill mode, abruptly did a right turn onto a side road.   No signal active and should have gone straight.    I rarely ever turn onto that road, so not like e.g. it was in recent driving logs.

gWM* and Nevada are unusable due to these inconsistencies for me.
I've had that behavior with most/all of the WM models. It feels like it's going to stop in the perfect spot then keeps inching forward, and I eventually brake manually.

Annoyingly it can do everything really well some of the time. On my 2024 ioniq 5 hda2 it has really good snap back on sharp turns, sometimes almost perfect. It's making me notice smaller things, like how steering changes when you go from flat to a slope up or down and the car doesn't react as well. Driving in San Francisco recently the car overcorrected on a right hand turn from a reasonably flat to a downward slope and it was a little shocking. I have noticed that on hills curves become a lot more difficult for the models to handle steering in general, both up and down. With the steering in general being so smooth and generally accurate, it's willingness to cut turns is pretty infuriating, especially since it seems perfectly capable of not needing to slow down to actually keep inside the lines while still holding the steering. 

Stop lights are usually aknowledged, but stopping ranges from far too early, to stopping perfectly at the line, to stopping close and creeping almost incessantly, to very abrupt and over. Most of the time starting at green is good, with the caveat that it doesn't start creeping before the green. Stop signs make me feel like I'm on a scooter delivering for doordash. 

the GWM models have always been pretty bad at not slipping off pavement onto soft (or hard) shoulders, or cutting in on other lanes so I'm hopefully that the occasionally shockingly perfect steering feel can come to other more reliably centered models
